pr_body:
This updates `WebApplicationBuilder` to only load `IConfigurationProvider`s once. Before this change, they would be loaded twice. Once by `Configurationmanager` and then again by the inner generic host's `ConfigurationBuilder`.

This causes problems with `StreamConfigurationSource`s like the one used by `builder.Configuration.AddJsonStream(jsonStream)` throwing errors similar to the following:

```
System.Text.Json.JsonReaderException
  HResult=0x80131500
  Message=The input does not contain any JSON tokens. Expected the input to start with a valid JSON token, when isFinalBlock is true. LineNumber: 0 | BytePositionInLine: 0.
  Source=System.Text.Json
  StackTrace:
   at System.Text.Json.ThrowHelper.ThrowJsonReaderException(Utf8JsonReader& json, ExceptionResource resource, Byte nextByte, ReadOnlySpan`1 bytes)
   at System.Text.Json.Utf8JsonReader.Read()
   at System.Text.Json.JsonDocument.Parse(ReadOnlySpan`1 utf8JsonSpan, JsonReaderOptions readerOptions, MetadataDb& database, StackRowStack& stack)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonDocument.Parse(ReadOnlyMemory`1 utf8Json, JsonReaderOptions readerOptions, Byte[] extraRentedArrayPoolBytes, PooledByteBufferWriter extraPooledByteBufferWriter)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonDocument.Parse(ReadOnlyMemory`1 json, JsonDocumentOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonDocument.Parse(String json, JsonDocumentOptions options)
   at Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Json.JsonConfigurationFileParser.ParseStream(Stream input)
   at Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Json.JsonStreamConfigurationProvider.Load(Stream stream)
   at Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.StreamConfigurationProvider.Load()
   at Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.ConfigurationRoot..ctor(IList`1 providers)
   at Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilder.Build()
   at Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.HostBuilder.BuildAppConfiguration()
   at Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.HostBuilder.Build()
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder.WebApplicationBuilder.Build()
```

Fixes #37030
Fixes #37046
pr_comments: I think this change might be too braking. Nothing looks at sources but lots of things look at providers. Having them wrapped is pretty breaking. For example GetDebugView is completely broken by this change

> I think this change might be too braking. Nothing looks at sources but lots of things look at providers. Having them wrapped is pretty breaking. For example GetDebugView is completely broken by this change

GetDebugView() is fixed pretty trivially by forwarding ToString() which I just did in [this commit](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/37039/commits/2570a38e09ab192ce12f61fc179c54f928486f11). Do you have examples of any code looking at the actual type of the providers @davidfowl?

I generally don't feel comfortable with wrapping providers because they  are exposed on IConfigurationRoot. I'm super paranoid about doing anything funky that changes the behavior after the service provider is built. There's too much code running not to break stuff

<!-- If this is a bug in Xamarin.Forms, please [open the issue in the Xamarin.Forms repo](https://github.com/xamarin/Xamarin.Forms/issues/new?assignees=&labels=s%2Funverified%2C+t%2Fbug+%3Abug%3A&template=bug_report.md&title=[Bug]+) -->

### Description
When configuring the host configuration from MauiProgram.cs, using the dotnet Core Generic Host. 
The exception "Stream was not readable" is thrown.

This bug appears when adding a MemoryStream to the configurationBuilder.

Below is an image of the locals from the de Microsoft.Maui.MauiAppBuilder, as you can see it tries to read the Memory Stream twice. Throwing a System.ObjectDisposedException the second time.

![MauiAppBugLocal png](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/74154010/133975590-e8f5902d-62e8-43d2-beb0-7c9e4b8ce9f1.jpg)


### Steps to Reproduce
I have added a reproduction link. For now it is added as a google drive link as I had trouble inserting the .zip file directly.
Sorry for the inconvenience.

### Expected Behavior
Configure the host configuration using the Memory Stream.

### Actual Behavior
MauiAppBuilder throws  System.ArgumentException: 'Stream was not readable.'

### Basic Information

- Version with issue: .NET MAUI Preview 8
- Last known good version: .NET MAUI Preview 7
- IDE: Visual Studio 2022 Preview 4
- Affected Devices:  Android 11.0 - API 30


### Reproduction Link
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1m2nfYmfDV2guJLfPAtlMJJupTHU57YH1/view?usp=sharing
comments: Hi @EliaCools , thank you for the bug report, this is certainly unexpected. Would you be able to post your repro app as a GitHub repo? We're not able to open other types of attachments.

Or, could you show what code you wrote to do this:

> This bug appears when adding a MemoryStream to the configurationBuilder.
Hello @Eilon Thank you for responding. I have made a repository for the bug reproduction. https://github.com/EliaCools/HostConfigBugReproduction/tree/main
OK I can confirm this repros for me. Will investigate.

The provided JSON stream is read once immediately when calling `configurationBuilder.AddJsonStream(stream)`, which leaves the stream's position at the end of the stream. Then when `MauiAppBuilder.Build()` is called, the internal ConfigurationBuilder tries to read the stream again, but it can't, because it's already at the end of the stream.

Interestingly, I tried the exact code in an ASP.NET Core app and I got the same results. So it seems that either for some bizarre reason this isn't _supposed_ to work (seems unlikely!), or there's a common bug either because we copied a bug, or the bug is in a shared type (e.g. something from MS.Extensions).

@Eilon @davidfowl @halter73 - do you think this needs to be fixed for 6.0?
I think a fix will need to be backported for 6.0. I'm looking into it now.

I plan to update [ConfigurationProviderSource](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/216c92b78bce31d5e81a70b589707ec2ae5ab21a/src/DefaultBuilder/src/WebApplicationBuilder.cs#L304-L317) to ignore the first call to `IConfigurationProvider.Load()` for all providers rather than special case `StreamConfigurationSources` since we know all the providers have been loaded by `ConfigurationManager` already. This also avoids regressing the behavior of `IConfigurationRoot.Reload()` which normally does throw an `InvalidOperationException` complaining "StreamConfigurationProviders cannot be loaded more than once."

I'll transfer this to https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore, but I'll submit PRs to both https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore and https://github.com/dotnet/maui with `release/6.0` backports.
Thank you @halter73 . Please tag me in those for review!

review_comments: Is there a functional difference with this change?

By changing the service descriptor from an instance to a factory, this gives the host ownership and now it disposes the ConfigurationManager. What's interesting is HostBuilder itself was using the same trick for its ConfigurationRoot and that no longer gets disposed, but it doesn't matter because ConfigurationManager took ownership of all the providers except the ChainedConfigurationSource to itself.

> but it doesn't matter because ConfigurationManager took ownership of all the providers except the ChainedConfigurationSource to itself.

What about the dangling change tokens?

Since all the providers get disposed, I would expect the change tokens to be unregistered from any filewatchers or anything like that (and manual testing confirms that). We could do a [similar trick to HostBuilder](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/3fa2860847df903b448d0af228b3362ca72480db/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting/src/HostBuilder.cs#L285) and call `Services.GetService<IEnumerable<IConfiguration>>()` to resolve both the HostBuilder's ConfgiruationRoot and WebApplicationBuilder's ConfigurationManager out of DI and ensure both get disposed. This will double-dispose providers added by tests or IHostingStartups, but that should be safe.
